stem: Meera takes a variegated leaf (with green and white patches) from her potted croton plant at home in Kochi. She keeps the plant in bright sunlight for six hours, then boils the leaf, removes the chlorophyll, and tests it with iodine solution. Which observation should she predict?

options.text: Both the green and white patches turn blue-black because the whole leaf was in sunlight
Only the green patches turn blue-black, showing starch formed only where chlorophyll received sunlight
Only the white patches turn blue-black because they absorb more sunlight
No patch turns blue-black because a variegated leaf cannot make starch

teacher.key_rationale: Starch is produced only where chlorophyll-containing tissue receives sunlight. The green patches have chlorophyll and were in sunlight, so they test blue-black with iodine; the white patches lack chlorophyll and show no starch. A is wrong because sunlight alone is insufficient without chlorophyll; C reverses the patches; D is false as green tissue can photosynthesise.
